response: Molecular genotype can provide useful information in the management of radioiodine refractory thyroid cancers. Specifically, patients with BRAF-mutant papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) have been found to have a significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) when treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) compared to those with BRAF wild-type. However, further investigations are required to fully understand the potential positive effect of BRAF mutations in radioiodine refractory thyroid cancer patients, as well as the negative prognostic impact in RAI-sensitive PTC patients. This suggests that molecular genotype may be a valuable tool in guiding treatment decisions for patients with radioiodine refractory thyroid cancers.
